title: Test action quality with counterfactual branches
doing: Proposed A5 uses the first12 eligible consumed sampled-K4 enemy-contact cases, four60/45/30/15frame offsets and eight continuation RNGs. Validate factual replay and full simulator/history/controller/held-phase restore parity, then compare K4-resume,K1 and a true12frame nine-action oracle over512frames. There are1152 continuations and432 cached oracle probes; no replacement cases or fresh cohort. A4 and this diagnostic share capture/rollout machinery but the deployable shield never receives oracle state.
expected: K1 may rescue a subset of late K4 contact deaths if reaction delay dominates; a12frame nine-action oracle may rescue cases where policy choices remain poor. If even earlier branches fail, finite-horizon local search cannot prove unavoidable death; earlier commitment and planning become stronger hypotheses.
why: These comparisons can distinguish local action-selection problems from earlier planning failures. They also suggest a route to better advantage estimates or training examples. The best simulated branch is a diagnostic reference using extra computation, not a deployable policy. Check full-game behavior before claiming an intervention improves survival.
next_step: Prepare and independently review snapshot/controller parity, branching design, seed registration and bounded exact-once gates before execution.
